geometry_edits.rationale: Wrap the courtyard mass in a profiled section logic so the upper mass and roof read as a deliberate program section rather than a flat extrusion.
Introduce a folded section family to give the mass a more coherent inhabited roof/upper profile without turning it into a tower.
Align the section profile with the long dimension so the mass reads as a street-oriented neighborhood building.
Strengthen the central void while preserving a substantial perimeter bar and active ground condition.

graph_edits.rationale: Keep the courtyard/public-threshold logic but make the void more legible and slightly stronger as a street-facing spatial figure.
Tighten the court so the remaining mass reads as a clearer inhabited perimeter with stronger hierarchy.
Preserve the access-aligned opening toward the verified public edge in the program frame.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent courtyard slab in plan and in at least two views, with a legible dominant mass and a meaningful internal void. The public threshold is reasonably responsive: the blue access edge is met by an open court/indented ground condition rather than a sealed blank wall. However, the section is too thin and too generic for the stated neighborhood-living brief. It behaves like a tallened extruded box with a carve, not a clearly inhabited 5-floor street building with active ground and calm upper hierarchy. The silhouette is mostly a simple slab with a notch; the stepped/courtyard principle is present but not yet programmatically rich enough to support the required mixed-use living contract. It is visually repaired and stable, but the massing still lacks convincing section-program integration and reads closer to a generic office/courtyard block than a capacity-aware neighborhood living form.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More tower-like and vertically emphatic than this compact neighborhood-living brief; the candidate should not drift toward a tall prism.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered massing with a strong singular datum can support mixed-use hierarchy when the lower edge remains legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office tower typology is a weak match for a low-rise street building; avoid importing the tower stance.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A slim, vertically differentiated profile can express upper hierarchy without fragmenting the whole.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is much smaller and more storefront-like; useful only for ground-edge logic, not overall massing.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple ground-level public threshold with a clear canopy/entry seam can strengthen street responsiveness.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Closer in spatial principle than the other references, but the candidate currently lacks the breadth and sectional richness of the precedent.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard and terrace logic can create public openness while preserving a coherent residential/mixed-use mass.

warnings: The form is coherent, but the section is underdeveloped for the program contract.
The current mass leans too much on generic extrusion plus courtyard subtraction.
Do not interpret the stepped roofline in the references as a mandate for a tower-like solution.
The open void is good, but it needs a clearer active ground/terrace reading tied to the access edge.
